hints: Use prefix sums so a subarray sum is a difference of two prefixes.
The DP transition is dp[g][i]=min over j<i of dp[g-1][j]+(P[i]-P[j])^2.
Expand the square to turn each j into a line queried at P[i].
analogy: Each previous cut offers a line; the cheapest line chooses the best place to start the current group.
example: For [1,2,3] split into 2 groups, [1,2] and [3] cost 9+9=18.
algorithm: For each group count g, scan endpoints i in increasing order. Maintain a minimum convex hull of lines with slope -2P[j] and intercept dp[g-1][j]+P[j]^2 for valid j<i; query at P[i] and add P[i]^2. Positive values make prefixes and query positions strictly increasing, enabling a monotone deque hull. Use wide integer arithmetic.
correctness: The algebraic expansion exactly equals the cost of choosing cut j. The hull retains the minimum over all valid cuts, so induction over groups and endpoints proves the DP values optimal.
complexity: For n values and k groups, O(kn) time and O(n) DP and hull space.
